title: Nvidia Breaks Revenue And Profit Records, And Will Keep Doing It
gist: Nvidia posted record Q3 FY2027 revenue of $115.8B and net income of $65.3B while its board confirmed Jensen Huang's resignation will not be reversed and installed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Guidance rose to $130B for Q4 and 75% growth for FY2028, with fast-growing ACIE (sovereign/neocloud/enterprise) customers poised to rival hyperscalers and a $2.5T cloud backlog.

insights.claim: Nvidia's board says Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned as president, CEO and board member after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, and the board does not intend to reinstate him.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Removes the founder-return overhang; key-person risk is now a governance question rather than a speculative one.
insights.quote: The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.
insights.locator: Nvidia’s first chairman of the board, Harvey Jones

insights.claim: Nvidia appointed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and retained Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search for a permanent chief executive.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Watch the permanent CEO pick as a signal of strategy continuity versus change.
insights.locator: Nvidia’s first chairman of the board, Harvey Jones

insights.claim: Timothy Prickett Morgan judges a Huang reinstatement highly unlikely, since it would require shareholders to vote out the current board in favor of one that would bring him back.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors should not price in a Huang comeback scenario.
insights.quote: Unless shareholders vote to throw out the current board of directors and vote in a board that tries to reinstate Huang. Which seems highly unlikely.
insights.locator: So, that’s that.

insights.claim: The author argues the Nvidia machine is self-sustaining without Huang: employees already know how to ramp Vera-Rubin systems now, ship Vera-Rubin Ultra next year, and deliver Feynman GPUs plus a presumed new CPU architecture in 2028.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Near-term roadmap execution is locked in; leadership change risk is more about the post-2028 era.

insights.claim: Interim CEO Colette Kress closed the earnings call asserting accelerating demand, growing supply and committed customers, partners and employees.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Management is deliberately projecting continuity to calm the market after the CEO exit.
insights.quote: Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing.

insights.claim: Nvidia posted record revenue of $115.8 billion in the quarter ended October 2026 (Q3 fiscal 2027), a little more than double the prior year's sales.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Growth is still accelerating at a $100B+ quarterly scale, undermining peak-cycle narratives.
insights.locator: In the quarter ended in October

insights.claim: Nvidia's net income in Q3 fiscal 2027 was $65.3 billion, or 56.4 percent of revenue, also more than doubling year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 56% net margin at this scale signals extreme pricing power with no sign of compression yet.
insights.locator: In the quarter ended in October

insights.claim: Nvidia ended Q3 fiscal 2027 with $97.7 billion in cash and investments, up 61.3 percent year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The balance sheet gives Nvidia ample firepower for buybacks, supply prepayments and ecosystem investments.
insights.locator: Nvidia ended Q3 F2027 with $97.7 billion

themes.theme: Capital return on an IBM-like scale

insights.claim: Nvidia returned $28 billion to shareholders in Q3 fiscal 2027: $22 billion in buybacks and $6 billion in dividends.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Shareholder returns are now a material EPS support mechanism.
insights.locator: Nvidia returned $28 billion back

insights.claim: Nvidia had $227 billion of remaining buyback authorization and added another $150 billion at quarter end, for $337 billion expected to be spent on buybacks before the end of fiscal 2028.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A ~$337B buyback program is a significant structural bid for the stock through FY2028.
insights.locator: Nvidia returned $28 billion back

insights.claim: The author draws a cautionary parallel to IBM, which took decades to spend that much on buybacks used to engineer earnings-per-share growth that rewarded Wall Street and executives with stock grants and bonuses.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Massive buybacks can mask organic growth deceleration later; watch the mix of EPS growth from buybacks vs operations.
insights.quote: It took IBM decades to blow that much dough on share buybacks to engineer its earnings per share
insights.locator: Nvidia returned $28 billion back

insights.claim: Nvidia's Compute & Networking group generated just under $106 billion in Q3 fiscal 2027, up 2.1X year on year and 20 percent sequentially, while the Graphics group posted a record $9.85 billion, up 61.5 percent.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Even the non-datacenter Graphics business is growing fast, though it is now under a tenth of revenue.

insights.claim: Nvidia's Datacenter Hyperscale division (hyperscalers, cloud builders and increasingly AI model builders like OpenAI and Anthropic) spent $60.14 billion with Nvidia in Q3 fiscal 2027, up 71.1 percent year on year and 23.5 percent sequentially.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler capex remains the largest single driver; AI labs are becoming hyperscaler-class buyers.
insights.locator: The Datacenter Hyperscale division is what

insights.claim: Nvidia's Datacenter AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise (ACIE) division, covering sovereign clouds, neoclouds, industrial firms, enterprises, governments and academia, had $47.47 billion in sales, up nearly 3X year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The non-hyperscaler customer base is growing far faster, diversifying Nvidia's customer concentration risk.
insights.locator: The Datacenter AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise

insights.claim: The author predicts that inference-focused ACIE customers will soon outspend the hyperscalers, cloud builders and AI model builders that made Nvidia rich.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A crossover would reduce dependence on a handful of hyperscalers and shift demand toward inference; track ACIE vs Hyperscale each quarter.
insights.quote: it probably will not be long before these ACIE customers, who are focused on inference, will do more spending than the hyperscalers
insights.locator: The Datacenter AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise

insights.claim: Nvidia restated its segment data this quarter after a neocloud's business model changed and it was reclassified as a cloud, moving it from the Datacenter Hyperscale division to ACIE.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Segment comparisons are subject to reclassification; use restated figures when tracking customer-mix trends.
